findings.title: Undefined 'closest alternative' scope in abstention

findings.title: No rule for children's personal data beyond the general PII rule
findings.problem: The Personal details section covers adults' identifiers but has no rule for data about children, even though the product domain includes child shoppers and the under-three rules exist; this belongs in the system prompt's Personal details section.
findings.fix: Add a rule in Personal details that the assistant never asks for, stores or repeats a child's name, age details or other identifiers beyond the age band needed for a product filter.

findings.title: Budget versus waved-aside amount rules are easy to confuse
findings.problem: Two budget rules sit side by side (a budget that stays a limit when the shopper invites going over, and an amount the shopper waves aside that is no limit) with no test stated for telling them apart.
findings.proof: An amount the shopper names and waves aside is no limit; the reply says which products cost more than it.
findings.fix: State one decision test in the Search rules (for example, whether the shopper says the amount is a limit) and reference it from both cases.

findings.title: Under-three rule restated in the age filter description
findings.problem: The rag.search description repeats the under-three rule in the loosening paragraph and again in the age_years parameter, so the same constraint is stated twice in the schema.
findings.proof: Never loosened: safety exclusions, a stated age range, a price floor, and the under-three rule
findings.fix: Keep the full under-three rule in the age_years parameter description and reference it briefly in the loosening paragraph.

findings.title: No worked example of a grounded table row or citation
findings.problem: The knowledge corpus defines the Ingredients and Rating cells but gives no example row showing how a cited statement, its source and its retrieval time should appear, which leaves cell format to inference.
findings.fix: Add one short example row for a catalog product and one for a live result to the catalog and sources file.

findings.title: No fallback if server-side instruction stripping misses text

findings.fix: Add a rule that any draft or tool-derived sentence containing imperative text aimed at the assistant is dropped by the rule checks.

metadata.role: voice shopping assistant for product discovery (recommends and compares products; it cannot buy, change or access anything)
metadata.business_case: A shopper speaks or types a request. The assistant searches a private product catalog (rag.search) and a live web search API (web.search) through one MCP server, then answers with a spoken summary of at most 15 seconds and an on-screen comparison table with citations. It has no accounts, no orders, no payments and no personal records; both tools are read-only.
metadata.goal: Recommend up to three products that fit what the shopper asked for, state only what the retrieved evidence states, cite a source for every product, keep the spoken reply short, refuse unsafe requests, and stay within product discovery.
